notes: SUMMARY: Large aerospace client evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for real-time chat and telemetry embedding workloads. Primary negotiation topic = SLA (uptime %, credits), maintenance windows, and P1/P2 support RTT.
Business priority: continuous availability for flight-ops assistant and telemetry reranking. Any downtime directly impacts operations & flight scheduling — high risk.
Deployment ask: Dedicated pool (8 reserved A100-eq) in NA region + private control plane (VPC) for telemetry PHI-ish metadata. Want ability to burst to extra capacity during peak launches.
Throughput targets: baseline 100 requests/sec (avg 40-60 tokens), P95 token latency target < 250ms on chat model, sustained throughput with KV cache reuse. Perf team provided sample traces.
Latency SLOs being negotiated: Stratacore requests 99.9% P95 latency under 250ms. Redwood standard offer: 99.5% with fallbacks. Customer pushing for 99.95-99.995% for critical routes.

Uptime & credits: Customer asked for 99.995% (approx 4 mthly downtime allowed ~2.6 min). Redwood initial SLA draft offers 99.9% for Dedicated with credits ramp: 99.0-99.9 -> 10% credit; 98.0-99.0 -> 25%; <98.0 -> 50%. Stratacore counters: require steeper credits and earlier thresholds (e.g., 99.95 floor).

Maintenance windows: Stratacore insists on scheduled maintenance only Sundays 02:00-05:00 PT max, advance notice 30 days for major upgrades, emergency maintenance require 4-hour notice and preferred fallback to non-critical region. Redwood wants 4-hour weekly windows across fleet for kernel and infra updates.

Support SLA: Customer requires 24/7 on-call with P1 response <= 15 minutes, P2 <= 1 hour, P3 <= 24 hours. Redwood standard Dedicated support: P1 30 min, P2 2 hours. SE working with SRE to evaluate on-call capacity and premium support add-on pricing.

Reserved GPU planning: Stratacore projection: 8 reserved A100-eq GPUs for steady state, plus ability to burst 4 GPUs for launch-day peaks. Finance concerned about cost delta for reserved vs burst. Suggested approach: hybrid reserved + cloud burst with explicit routing policy and cost cap alerts.

Model variants & fallback: Need policy for automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant when capacity constrained, but business mandates no quality regression >5% on reranking metrics. Redwood suggested canary + A/B rollout and rollback on evaluation metrics.

Security/legal: Requires SOC2 type II + ISO27001 in contract, KMS integration, detailed audit logging retention 7 years for specific telemetry logs. Data residency: primary data must remain in NA; backups can be multi-region under NDA.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-04): 'We will accept planned maintenance only if we can guarantee failover and less than 30s tail latency impact on critical routes.'
Procurement path: Legal -> Security review -> Exec signoff. Procurement timetable tight: aiming to close by 2026-04 to align with summer launch schedule.
Stated blockers in last meeting: legal SLA language on credit calculation, clarity on how uptime measured per-route vs per-cluster, and cost of premium 15-min P1 support.
Next technical milestone: POC load test week of 2026-03-22 to validate 100 rps baseline and cold-start token latency under quantized model. SE to provide perf harness and initial kernel config.

Action items: (1) Redwood to produce redlined SLA draft with two alternative uptime tiers + credit tables; (2) SRE to estimate cost delta for 15-min P1 coverage; (3) Schedule maintenance window working session with Stratacore ops.
